extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, and Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) staff
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order implementing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24: describes legal authority, respondent's procedural obligations, grounds for discipline, the imposed suspension and its conditions, publication and notice requirements, and reinstatement procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), the suspension of Respondent from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO or Office) for a period of three (3) years is hereby ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59; the Director may impose discipline identical to that imposed by a state court when the prerequisites of § 11.24 are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's opportunity to contest (response requirement and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order directed that if Respondent seeks to contest imposition of his suspension from practice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), Respondent shall file, within 40 days, a response containing all information Respondent believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that the imposition of discipline identical to that imposed by the Supreme Court of the State of New York would be unwarranted based upon any of the grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The response must contain all information to establish a genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d)(1); failure to file a response supports a Director determination that no genuine issue exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for imposing identical discipline when no genuine issue exists
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), suspension of Respondent from practice before the USPTO for a period identical to that imposed by the state is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director determines both (1) whether a genuine issue of material fact exists and (2) whether identical discipline is appropriate; a lack of contesting response allows imposition of identical discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for discipline: violation of ethical standard (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: The suspension was ordered for violation of the ethical standard set out in 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites the underlying state disciplinary findings that respondent engaged in illegal conduct that adversely reflected on his honesty, trustworthiness, or fitness as a lawyer (state Code of Professional Responsibility DR 1-102[A][3] and DR 1-102[A][7]); such conduct supports discipline under the cited USPTO regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and effective date of suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the Office for a period of three (3) years. The imposed suspension begins on January 22, 2010.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order implements the duration imposed by the state court (three years) and reflects any state-specified conditions (the state order also referenced 'or until the expiration of his criminal term of probation, whichever is longer').

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to wind up matters (30-day limited practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office beginning on the date of this Final Order and expiring thirty (30) days after the date of this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the period of limited recognition the Respondent is directed to wind up all client business before the Office and to withdraw from employment in all pending proceedings in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 10.40.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to withdraw and wind up client matters (37 C.F.R. § 10.40)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is directed, during the time of his limited recognition, to wind up all client business before the Office and to withdraw from employment in all pending proceedings in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 10.40.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent must take the steps specified by § 10.40 for withdrawal and winding up client matters (notification, transfer of files, protection of client interests).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on accepting new clients during limited recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is directed not to accept any new clients having business before the Office during the 30 days of limited recognition afforded by this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The limited recognition period is strictly for winding up existing matters; accepting new matters during that time is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish this Final Order; the OED Director shall publish the following notice in the Official Gazette: [full notice text identifying Respondent, registration number, suspension for three years, statutory/regulatory citations, and factual basis].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must include the reasons for discipline, statutory citations (35 U.S.C. § 32; 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59), and factual summary; disciplinary decisions are posted at the OED Reading Room (URL provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with duties during suspension (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.58 prescribes duties and obligations of suspended practitioners (e.g., obligations regarding representation, notifications, and restrictions) which must be followed during the suspension period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of public discipline to other jurisdictions and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted to practice, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director has an affirmative duty to notify other regulatory bodies and courts of the discipline and its basis as specified in § 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement compliance (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement requests must satisfy the procedural and substantive requirements set out in § 11.60 (e.g., proof of rehabilitation, compliance with prior conditions); the Order references that the state reinstatement was conditioned on an independent psychiatric evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of the Final Order (certificate of service and address requirements under § 11.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order was mailed first class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the Respondent at the address provided to OED pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11 (and to an address at which the OED Director believes Respondent receives mail).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service must follow mailing procedures and use addresses maintained under § 11.11; the Certificate of Service documents compliance with service requirements.
